summary: Found two complementary external assessment resources for synthetic training: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS measures for teamwork and diagnostic-improvement learning, and a peer-reviewed pediatric H&P rubric with example answer keys. Neither supplies New Brunswick hospital-specific learning outcomes or performance estimates. These are discovery candidates; no dataset or instrument was acquired.

sources.title: TeamSTEPPS Measurement Tools
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
sources.geography: United States; institution or unit level, not New Brunswick-specific
sources.period: TeamSTEPPS 3.0 materials; source page last reviewed January 2024
sources.grain: Questionnaire item/response; observed team behavior by domain; scenario learning-benchmark question and answer
useful_fields: T-TAQ: 30 items on team structure, leadership, situation monitoring, mutual support, and communication, using 5-point Likert scales
T-TPQ: 35-item, 5-point Likert self-report on the same five domains
Team Performance Observation Tool: ratings of team structure, communication, leadership, and situation monitoring
Learning Benchmarks: questions with best-answer discussion for scenarios
observed_facts: AHRQ describes T-TAQ as usable before and after training to assess teamwork attitudes.
AHRQ says the Team Performance Observation Tool can assess recommended behaviors during simulations.
AHRQ cautions that short-term attitude change does not establish behavior or outcome change.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Inspect the linked official PDFs and record their version/date, item wording, scoring instructions, and any reuse terms before adapting. For a bounded prototype, map a small set of rubric criteria to observable actions in one synthetic team scenario, keeping case facts separate from expected behaviors.
limitations: National/external instrument; no local RWJUH, Saint Peter's, Middlesex County, or facility-level observations.
Questionnaire and observation scores are not patient outcomes or clinical correctness measures.
The source page establishes public access but no explicit license or redistribution terms; verify rights before reproducing items.

sources.title: TeamSTEPPS for Diagnosis Improvement Course
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
sources.geography: United States; externally developed training resource, no New Brunswick-specific data
sources.grain: Course module or case exercise × learning objective; team assessment response; 20-item knowledge assessment response
useful_fields: Seven customizable learning modules: diagnostic team structure, communication, leadership, situation monitoring, mutual support, and synthesis
Team Assessment Tool for Improving Diagnosis, used to identify areas to prioritize and track perceptions over time
Post-course knowledge assessment: 20 questions; response key is in the Facilitator's Guide
Case-based scenarios and reflective exercises in the Participant Workbook
observed_facts: AHRQ describes the course as training multidisciplinary diagnostic teams, including nonclinicians, patients, and families.
The course offers a reality-based diagnostic journey case for discussion and a 20-question knowledge assessment.
The source page links the materials but does not establish a license for redistribution.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Open the official workbook, assessment, and facilitator guide linked from the page; document version, objective-to-item mapping, answer key location, and permissions. If rights permit, catalog source materials separately before creating a local adaptation; keep all case-specific facts synthetic and approval pending.
limitations: Training curriculum is not a local outcome dataset or calibrated clinical gold standard.
The linked answer key is inside the Facilitator's Guide; do not claim it acquired based on the discovery page alone.
Applicability to the two named hospitals and county requires domain-owner review.

sources.title: Self-Directed Rater Training for Pediatric History and Physical Exam Evaluation (P-HAPEE) Rubric, a Validated Written H&P Assessment Tool
sources.publisher: MedEdPORTAL / Association of American Medical Colleges
sources.geography: United States medical education; pediatric clerkship context, not New Brunswick-specific
sources.period: Published 2017; implementation evidence described through fall 2016
sources.grain: Written pediatric H&P × rubric criterion × rater score; sample H&P × detailed scoring key
useful_fields: Two sample H&Ps with detailed scoring keys
Reported validity and rater-training evidence; study included 23 attending physicians and senior residents
observed_facts: The publication page lists the rubric, sample H&Ps, detailed answer keys, and rater-training booklet as appendices.
The authors report a formative pediatric written-H&P assessment use case and caution that higher-stakes use would need additional rater calibration.
The resource's pediatric scope makes it unsuitable as a general all-age rubric without adaptation and review.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Review the appendices and verify file-level reuse permissions. If permitted and the scenario is pediatric, catalog the rubric and answer-key files as separate source records, then test whether each criterion can be applied to the chosen synthetic case without filling unknown facts.
limitations: Pediatric written documentation rubric; not an acute-care scenario benchmark for all learners or patient populations.
Published evidence is from external training programs and does not estimate local learner performance.
The publication page is public, but the opened evidence does not establish redistribution rights for appendix files.

missing_inputs: No observed pre/post learner scores, rubric ratings, or scenario outcomes for RWJUH CCN310038, Saint Peter's CCN310070, or Middlesex County were found in this bounded search.
No locally approved learning objectives, faculty-reviewed answer keys, or assessment approval scope were identified.
Instrument reuse and redistribution terms require verification before copying or adapting item text.
simulation_use: Treat these sources as candidate scaffolds for case-version × disclosure/assertion × objective × rubric/evidence records. Use AHRQ materials for observable teamwork behaviors and knowledge-check structure; consider P-HAPEE only for a pediatric written-H&P case. Keep source facts, synthetic case assertions, learner responses, and evaluator judgments separate. Label all locally authored mappings as proposed and faculty approval pending; do not infer local clinical facts or expected performance from external materials.
limitations: This was source discovery only: no downloads, extraction, cataloging, or acquisition occurred.
Search scope was limited to two searches and four opened primary-source pages.
No source provides a local calibration benchmark for the named hospitals or county.
Public availability does not by itself establish permission to redistribute or reuse instrument content.
